### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57cde8cb3da5970f2c3f6512569cacdb9b2b06a8`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57cde8cb3da5970f2c3f6512569cacdb9b2b06a8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0ea4b0fb7cdec4dc0e98684a9062e2c0a38a4327` — the merge of head `ffba862a673281d0828ea9fa2ec7fc6c403c97fc` into base `57cde8cb3da5970f2c3f6512569cacdb9b2b06a8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0ea4b0fb7cdec4dc0e98684a9062e2c0a38a4327 && git checkout 0ea4b0fb7cdec4dc0e98684a9062e2c0a38a4327
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 57cde8cb3da5970f2c3f6512569cacdb9b2b06a8 ffba862a673281d0828ea9fa2ec7fc6c403c97fc && git checkout -B drift-repro 57cde8cb3da5970f2c3f6512569cacdb9b2b06a8 && git merge --no-ff ffba862a673281d0828ea9fa2ec7fc6c403c97fc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57cde8cb3da5970f2c3f6512569cacdb9b2b06a8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 57cde8cb3da5970f2c3f6512569cacdb9b2b06a8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. `engine.aggregate` refuses `{ field, dateGranularity }` over a field whose declared type is in `SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES` (exactly `formula`), whatever its `returnType`, with `INVALID_FIELD` / 400, `path groupBy.N.dateGranularity`, `param groupBy`, `field`, `fields`, `object`, before any driver is asked — RIGHT. The door sits at the aggregate entry (engine.ts 21291) ahead of both `drv.aggregate` (21680) and `applyInMemoryAggregation` (21725), so every engine caller gets it: REST `/data/:object/query` and its dispatcher twin through `findData` (the test file's REST-door case pins this door's throw reaching the wire through `findData`, on a text bucket; the formula arm is the same throw from the same door), the MCP `aggregate_records` bridge, a flow or hook, and the analytics ObjectQL strategy. The predicate is the spec's one judgment of virtuality, the same one the sort (sortability.zod.ts category 3), filter (`filter-dotted-head.ts` 'virtual'), search (`search-fields.ts`) and value-aggregate (`aggregate-field-type-compatibility.ts`) axes read; no local type list.
2. The arm runs BEFORE the class reading, in both doors — RIGHT and load-bearing: `classOfDeclaredType('formula')` returns `undefined` (having-filter.ts 1151), so an arm after it would have been skipped; the dev's ablation 3 shows the service copy falls through to the wrong sentence when the order is lost. The service copy's `type !== undefined && isVirtualSearchField({ type })` is the same predicate as the engine's `isVirtualSearchField(declared)` (both read `typeof type === 'string'`).
3. The SQL live faces (`/analytics/query` both compositions, the cube path) keep `INVALID_FIELD` / 400 but gain the located envelope and a correct remedy in place of the driver's missing-column backstop and its "run schema sync" prescription — RIGHT; the accept set there does not move, only the sentence.
4. An engine with no native `aggregate` (in-memory aggregation) stops serving one `null` group — RIGHT; this is the real narrowing on the engine, and the CONTROL line that pinned the null group as served is the behaviour the ruling retires.
5. The `/analytics/sql` dry run (objectql-strategy.ts 806, on `echoGroupBy`, direct or cross-object keys) and the draft preview (analytics-service.ts 2921) refuse with the same sentence — RIGHT. The two message templates were compared textually: byte-identical apart from the `return` wrapper. A dataset dimension declaring `dateGranularity: 'month'` over a formula reaches the same keys through `aggregateGroupKeys`, so it is refused on every face too (pinned).
6. Unchanged, as declared: a date or datetime bucket; an undeclared field or a registry-less host (engine) and a host wiring no `sourceFieldMeta` (service) stay unjudged; plain `groupBy` over a formula stays #29304's. No export, public member, answer member, error code or status is added: `virtualDateBucketMessage` and `dateBucketRefusal` are module-private; `isVirtualSearchField` is already exported from `@objectstack/spec/data` (index 362) and both packages already depend on `@objectstack/spec` at runtime.
7. The refusal sentence hardcodes "A formula field is virtual" while the predicate is the set — acceptable today (`search-fields.test.ts` pins the set to exactly `['formula']`), noted as should-fix only if the set ever grows; no runtime string carries a tracker number.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql: patch`, `@objectstack/service-analytics: patch` — RIGHT: `Metadata-protocol: none` (no authorable key, value or meaning moves) takes `patch` per AGENTS.md; the BREAKING banner and `!` summary stay, and the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker was accepted by `check-adr-0087-registration` on this head (one declared-breaking changeset, disposition present). Both packages are published (neither `private`). The new changeset is issue-scoped in name.

`Clause-②:` line. The ARM is right: `(narrowing)` on the changeset decides the narrowing face, and the ADR-0087 step read it (`[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing]`). Two flags on the line itself:

- MUST-FIX (PR body, no push): the PR body's declaration line names the key twice (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — … (The seat ruling 6575980095 sets this line; it supersedes the claim's Clause-②: no.)`), which the fleet's one reader (`clause2-line.mjs`, `clause2LineDescribes`) triages as a `describing` near miss, not a declaration. On this head the `Guard against accidental major bumps` step therefore reports `LEVEL AXIS: NOT MEASURED — the Clause-②: line was not readable` and exits red: a second, UNDESIGNED red inside the `Check Changeset` failure, beside the designed one in ③. Remedy: move the supersession note to a line of its own that does not spell the key (e.g. "The seat ruling 6575980095 sets the declaration above; it supersedes the claim's earlier `no`."); the gate re-reads the body on `edited` with no push. The changeset's line names the key once and reads as declared.
- SHOULD-FIX, escalated to the seat: the VALUE `yes` is defined by the reader as "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another"; the body says "Nothing is widened", so the truthful spelling for this shape is `no (narrowing)` (the one #28977's changeset carries and the one `record-recognisers` keys the narrowing face on). The seat ruling ordered `yes (narrowing)`, so this is the seat's call; the level is unaffected (it follows `Metadata-protocol` alone) and the face is unaffected (any `(narrowing)` arm decides it). Changing it needs a push to the changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question (confirm the DELIBERATE CORRECTION of #28977's pending changeset): CONFIRMED, option A. The edit is correct — the base sentence "A field with no declared type, or a `formula`, is not judged, as in the engine." is made false by this head on every face; the new sentence states the new truth and points at this card — and minimal: one sentence in one bullet, frontmatter, declaration lines, BREAKING banner, remedy and the preview paragraph untouched; that changeset's own `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` stays right for its dry-run narrowing. The `Check Changeset` log on this head shows the foreign-changeset refusal naming exactly that file as the two-class DELIBERATE CORRECTION / COLLISION shape; the remedy the gate prescribes (say so on the PR, get it confirmed, do NOT restore, do NOT label `skip-changeset`) is met by the PR body's Verification section plus this record. The gate's own text says `Check Changeset` is not a required context, so that designed red blocks no merge. Option B (two contradicting pending notes in one release) is refused.
- Dev deviation "Clause-② yes (narrowing) per seat ruling": see ② (arm right; value escalated; PR-body line unreadable).
- Dev deviation "edited another PR's pending changeset": confirmed above.
- Dev deviation "base f125ce40, main moved 40 commits, none touching the seven paths": VERIFIED — `git log f125ce40..origin/main` over the seven PR paths is empty; over the cited files only engine.ts moved (344a16d7, stored-reference update, not the aggregate doors).
- Forced test edits: exactly the two the ruling accepted when named, and both are named in the body — the CONTROL formula "resolves" line removed with the read count 6 to 5 and the title trimmed; the #28977 formula-skip case replaced by the refusal case with the header note rewritten. Right: both pinned the behaviour the ruling retires.
- Dogfood deviation (first attempt mis-flagged `--concurrency`): the rerun's VERDICT is reported on this head; not re-run here.
- Check-runs on `cae03ff5` (conclusions as read): at 12:50Z, 47 runs: 30 success, 13 skipped, 1 failure (`Check Changeset`), 3 still in progress (`Test Core` shards 3/8, 5/8 and 6/8; shards 1, 2, 4, 7, 8 and `Build Core` concluded success). Green so far include `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check PR Size`, every `Type Check` and `Lint` job, `Test UI` and `Live E2E UI`. The three open shards must conclude green before any landing; this record does not claim them. `Check Changeset` is red with TWO red steps: `Reject an empty-frontmatter changeset added by this PR` (the designed foreign-changeset refusal, confirmed above) and `Guard against accidental major bumps` (undesigned: the unreadable PR-body declaration, the must-fix in ②). The dev's report accounts for the first only; a local run of `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` has no event payload and exits 0 by design (its own battery: "reddening it would refuse a developer who has no PR body to fix"), which is why the second never showed in the dev's 62-green local run. Only CI reads the body.
- Out-of-scope findings the dev carried (#29304, plain groupBy over a formula): right to keep out; the ruling scoped this card to the date bucket.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing is read against the published spec on `main`. Does it take a declared capability away at the consumer? No. Nothing on `main` declares a formula date-bucketable: `GroupByNodeSchema` says `dateGranularity` buckets "date values"; `search-fields.ts` declares a `formula` VIRTUAL ("no driver materialises a column"), `driver-sql`'s `fieldHasColumn` emits none, and the sort, filter, search and value-aggregate axes already refuse it on that ground; `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/dashboards.md` says a formula "has no column: refused whatever its `returnType` says"; no example app, dataset or cube buckets one. Does it make the spec's own refusal real? Yes: the three measured answers (a driver backstop with a wrong prescription, a `null` group that looked served, SQL for a statement that never runs) were never a delivered capability but an implementation gap at an axis the engine door explicitly skipped, and the ruling retires it at the engine where the other axes judge virtuality, with the service's one existing copy following field for field. Not a capability narrowed at the consumer. The authoring surface is consistent with that: `DatasetSchema` accepts a dimension `type: 'date'` over any column path and the compiler maps it to `time` without judging the source field (dataset-compiler.ts 550), so an authored formula bucket is refused at query time exactly as #28977's text dimension is; no authoring-time door is owed by this card.

Doors probed for a second answer: REST and dispatcher aggregate, MCP, flow/hook: engine door. Analytics query and cube, both compositions: `NativeSQLStrategy.canHandle` declines every bucketed time dimension (native-sql-strategy.ts 645), so the ObjectQL strategy (priority 20) hands the engine the keys: engine door. Saved dataset run: the same live path through `DatasetExecutor` and `service.query`. Dry run, direct and cross-object echo: service door on the same keys. Draft preview: service door. A dataset dimension's declared granularity: `aggregateGroupKeys` honours it, same doors. Driver-sql, mongodb and turso native aggregates sit behind the engine door. Virtual kinds: `SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES` is exactly `formula`; `summary` and `autonumber` are computed-but-stored with real columns and are not touched by this arm.

Findings:
- MUST-FIX (② above): the PR body's `Clause-②:` line is unreadable, so the level axis was not measured in CI on this head and `Check Changeset` carries an undesigned red. A body edit, no push; a fresh record on this same head can then PASS.
- SHOULD-FIX (seat's call, ②): `yes (narrowing)` where nothing widens; `no (narrowing)` is the reader's spelling for this shape.
- SHOULD-FIX, own card (not this PR's): `FallbackDelegateStrategy` (priority 30, reached only on a host whose engine cannot aggregate) delegates a cube query to `MemoryAnalyticsService`, which folds time dimensions itself (memory-analytics.ts 1172 onward) with no field-type reading and neither door in front of it; a formula bucket there still lands in one `null` group. Outside the ruling's three faces and unmeasured here; the seat may file it beside #29304.
- Note: a cross-object time dimension over a related object's field hands the engine only the FK column, so neither door reads the related field's type; pre-existing since #28852 for every non-date type, not this card's, unmeasured here.
- Note (①.7): the sentence hardcodes "A formula field" while the predicate is the set; harmless while the set is pinned to `formula`.
